newsitem.title: USA: SEC says insider trading charges settled.
newsitem.headline: SEC says insider trading charges settled.

text.p: A Hong Kong man settled insider trading charges involving Renaissance Hotel Group N.V. shares and agreed to pay a $2 million penalty, the Securities and Exchange Commission said Thursday.
Without admitting or denying wrong-doing, Frederick Liu, 35, also agreed to an order barring him from repeating the alleged offences, the SEC said.

In its complaint, filed in federal court in New York, the SEC alleged that Liu purchased 1.4 million Renaissance common shares on Dec. 30 and 31, prior to an announcement that Doubletree Corp. had reached an agreement to acquire Renaissance.
The SEC alleged Liu purchased the shares at an average cost of $15.66 each for a potential profit of $11.3 million.

However, Liu subsequently learned that the SEC had authorised an emergency lawsuit charging him with illegal insider trading, and he cancelled the stock trades and abandoned the trading profits, the agency said.
The SEC did not disclose how Liu learned of the pending acquisition announcement.
The agency is seeking just the $2 million penalty because Liu never collected on the profits, Isenberg said.
The merger between Renaissance and Doubletree was never finalised and Renaissance has since been acquired by Marriott International Inc.
